# Example 2: Box Model

#### Course: Learn CSS

## Example 2: Box Model

Consider a button on a webpage:

```html
1<h3>Simple button</h3>
2<a href="#">Click Me!</a>
3<p>The button says "Click Me!"</p>
```

```css
1a {
2    /* Box model properties */
3    padding: 10px;
4    border: 2px solid black;
5    margin: 30px;
6
7    display: block;    /* Required for width/height */
8    width: 120px;
9    height: 30px;
10
11    /* Other styles */
12    text-align: center;
13    background-color: #2596be;
14    color: #ffffff;
15    text-decoration: none;
16}
```

Browser Output

![Box Model Example](data:image/png;base64,)

The <a> element here looks like a button, because it is styled like that using box model properties.

Like the previous example, this element can also be broken down into:

![Box Model Breakdown](data:image/png;base64,)
